items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Like eventually be a Bill Bailey -- after Terry Wilson discovered him he went away for about -- about four weeks on his own somewhere

ctx.x: All the other dancers you didn't find that --

No -- I -- I enjoyed them immensely, but I'm saying they weren't an influence on me -- well, there was two more, there was Raymond Winfield and Walter Beaty, you know. I had my moments, too, you know. I was -- I would rather do an original work than try to do something -- an impression of another tap dancer, see. It's like introducing a new degree to tap dancing. Eventually you can create -- you can introduce a creation, see. Like eventually be a Bill Bailey -- after Terry Wilson discovered him he went away for…

turn, you see. And he had ways of doing -- performing that was infectious to other people that especially was in the same art -- tap dancing, you know. Well, the fraternity used to call them desserts -- like the end of the meal you have the sweets, you know, and that's the way they used to appear, you know. It was like a refreshment, you know.
